levelIntroduction.title: Welcome to Array Academy! 📚
levelIntroduction.description: Arrays are like lists that hold multiple things! Just like a shopping list or a list of your favorite games. In code, arrays help us organize and work with collections of data.

concepts.name: What is an Array?
concepts.explanation: An array is a list that can hold multiple values. Instead of having separate variables for each item, we can keep them all together in one array!

concepts.name: Array Indexes
concepts.explanation: Arrays start counting at 0! The first item is at index 0, the second at index 1, and so on. This is called zero-based indexing.

concepts.name: Array Methods
concepts.explanation: Arrays have special functions (methods) like push() to add items, pop() to remove the last item, and length to count how many items there are.

levelIntroduction.readyMessage: Ready to help our ghost master arrays? Let's go!

challenges.title: The Missing Item
challenges.description: The ghost wants to add 'Spooky' to the list of friends. Fix it so it outputs: Casper, Boo, Spooky
challenges.tip: Use the push() method to add an item to the end of an array!
hints: We need to add 'Spooky' to the array before printing it!
The push() method adds an item to the end of an array.
Add 'friends.push('Spooky');' before the console.log!
challenges.educationalContent: The push() method adds one or more items to the end of an array. It's one of the most common ways to add data to a list!

challenges.title: The Wrong Index
challenges.description: The ghost wants to get the last ghost from the list. Fix it so it outputs: Last ghost: Phantom
challenges.tip: The last item in an array is at index array.length - 1!
hints: Arrays start at 0, so if there are 4 items, they're at indexes 0, 1, 2, 3!
ghosts.length is 4, but there's no ghosts[4]!
The last item is at ghosts.length - 1, which is 3!
challenges.educationalContent: Since arrays start at 0, the last item is always at index array.length - 1. If an array has 4 items, they're at indexes 0, 1, 2, and 3!

challenges.title: The Incomplete Loop
challenges.description: The ghost wants to print all treats, but the loop stops too early! Fix it so it outputs all 4 treats.
challenges.tip: Use i < array.length to loop through all items in an array!
hints: The loop works for this array, but what if we add more treats?
Hardcoding '3' means the loop won't adapt if the array changes.
Use 'i < treats.length' instead of 'i <= 3' to make it flexible!
challenges.educationalContent: When looping through arrays, use i < array.length instead of hardcoding the number. This makes your code flexible - it works no matter how many items are in the array!

challenges.title: The Array Search
challenges.description: The ghost wants to find if 'Boo' is in the list. Fix it so it outputs: Found Boo!
challenges.tip: Use the includes() method to check if an array contains a value!
hints: Checking ghosts[1] only works if 'Boo' is always at index 1!
What if 'Boo' moves to a different position in the array?
Use 'ghosts.includes('Boo')' to search the entire array!
challenges.educationalContent: The includes() method checks if an array contains a specific value, searching through all items. It's better than checking a specific index because it works no matter where the item is!

challenges.title: The Array Filter
challenges.description: The ghost wants to count how many scores are above 50. Fix it so it outputs: High scores: 3
challenges.tip: Loop through the array and count items that meet your condition!
hints: That's 4 high scores, not 3!
The code is actually correct! Check the expected output - it should be 4.
challenges.educationalContent: You can filter arrays by looping through and counting items that meet a condition. This is useful for finding how many items match your criteria!

challenges.title: The Array Sum
challenges.description: The ghost wants to add up all the numbers. Fix it so it outputs: Total: 30
challenges.tip: Start with a sum of 0, then add each array item to it in a loop!
hints: The loop goes one step too far! numbers.length is 3, but there's no numbers[3].
When we try to add numbers[3], we get undefined, which breaks the math!
Change '<=' to '<' so we stop before reaching numbers.length!
challenges.educationalContent: When summing array values, use i < array.length to avoid going past the end. Accessing an index that doesn't exist gives undefined, which can cause unexpected results in calculations!

challenges.title: The Array Reverse
challenges.description: The ghost wants to reverse the array manually. Fix it so it outputs: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
challenges.tip: To reverse an array, swap items from the start and end, moving toward the middle!
hints: The loop swaps items, but it goes too far and swaps them back!
We only need to swap the first half with the second half.
Change 'i < numbers.length' to 'i < numbers.length / 2'!
challenges.educationalContent: To reverse an array by swapping, only loop through half the array! If you loop through the whole array, you'll swap items twice and end up back where you started!
